title: Semiconductors and packages for RF
blurb: Explain why GaAs and GaN suit UHF and microwaves, what MMICs are, and why surface mount beats leaded packages at RF.

E6E01.why: GaAs has **higher electron mobility**, so devices respond faster at UHF and above.
E6E01.trap: Higher noise figures and lower transconductance would be drawbacks.

E6E02.why: A **DIP** has pins that pass through holes in the board. PLCC, BGA and SOT mount on the surface.
E6E02.trap: BGA, PLCC and SOT are all surface-mount.

E6E03.why: Gallium nitride supports the **highest frequency** of operation for MMICs among these.
E6E03.trap: Silicon nitride and dioxide are insulators, not the fast active material.

E6E04.why: MMICs are designed for **50 Ω** input and output, matching standard RF systems.
E6E04.trap: 75 Ω is video and cable-TV practice; 300 Ω is old twin-lead.

E6E05.why: Noise figure is a small positive dB value; a good low-noise UHF preamp is about **0.5 dB**.
E6E05.trap: Negative dB and dBm values are not noise figures.

E6E06.why: MMICs give **controlled gain, low noise figure and constant input and output impedance** across their range.
E6E06.trap: Nearly infinite gain is an ideal op-amp idea, not an MMIC trait.

E6E07.why: MMICs connect through **microstrip**: copper traces on the board forming a controlled-impedance line.
E6E07.trap: Waveguide and parallel wire do not suit tiny printed-board parts.

E6E08.why: DC bias enters through a **resistor and/or RF choke on the output lead**, which keeps RF out of the supply.
E6E08.trap: Feeding the input lead or a bare Vcc pin is not how the common MMIC works.

E6E09.why: **Surface-mount** parts have the shortest leads, so the least parasitic L and C.
E6E09.trap: Axial, radial and TO-220 packages all have long leads.

E6E10.why: Surface mount gives a smaller area, shorter traces, and **less parasitic inductance and capacitance**: all three are true.
E6E10.trap: Each option is a real advantage; none is wrong.

E6E11.why: **DIP** = dual in-line package: two rows of pins on opposite sides.
E6E11.trap: It does not mean two chips in the package.

E6E12.why: DIP leads are long, adding stray inductance that wrecks performance at UHF and higher: **excessive lead length**.
E6E12.trap: Dielectric loss and conductive epoxy are not the issue.
